page: Microsoft Azure M32ls is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical Intel Xeon 8280L cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 256.0 GB, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Storage is provided via a bundled 1049 GB local SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance dichotomy. Single-core performance is consistently positioned in the bottom 10% across stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests like gzip and bzip3. However, the server compensates with its multi-core capabilities, achieving average tier results in multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth, both cached and uncached, remains in the average tier, with uncached read speeds reaching 106.6 GB/sec. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput also align with middle-tier expectations.

Positioned as a low-memory variant within the MS family, the M32ls offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without the premium cost of higher-tier memory-optimized instances. Given its average multi-threaded performance and 256 GB RAM, it is well-suited for relational databases, Redis caching layers, multi-threaded data processing, and moderate web serving workloads. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or heavy LLM inference, where its single-core and large-model processing speeds fall into the lower percentiles.
